name: Granpai3DGlobe
author: Granpai

sections.description:
Granpai3DGlobe drops a genuine, rotating WebGL 3D globe (or a flat world map) anywhere on your site with a single shortcode – no Google Maps API key, no per-load billing, no external tracking scripts. Add a pin for every office, store, event, or team member, and each one opens a clean modal with its own heading and text when clicked.

Who is this for?

  • Multi-location businesses that want a store/office locator that actually looks impressive, not a plain embedded map
  • Agencies and teams building an “our global presence” or “where we work” page
  • Travel, real estate, or events sites that need to plot places on a map
  • Nonprofits and NGOs showing where their projects or chapters operate

Core features (Free)

  • Real 3D Globe mode (WebGL, drag-to-rotate, scroll/pinch to zoom) or a Flat map mode for a more traditional look
  • Dark or Light theme, independent of map mode
  • Photoreal (satellite imagery), Minimal (clean line-art), or Night Lights globe style
  • Custom pin color per map, and choice of which side the pin panel docks on (desktop)
  • Next / Previous navigation between pins in the modal, with an animated flight-line arc tracing the path between them
  • A “Get Directions” button on every pin (on by default, toggle per pin) – auto-builds a Google Maps link from the pin’s own coordinates, no API key needed
  • Unlimited maps and pins are a Pro feature – Free includes 1 map with up to 5 pins, so you can fully evaluate the plugin before upgrading
  • One simple shortcode: [Granpai3DGlobe id="123"]
  • Import / Export your maps and pins as JSON – move between sites or keep a backup
  • No API key required, no recurring third-party map billing

Pro add-on (sold separately)

  • Unlimited maps and pins
  • Two additional globe or flat map styles: Dot Matrix and Low-Poly
  • Pin images and contact/social icons (email, phone, website, Facebook, X, Instagram, LinkedIn) shown right in the pin’s modal, plus a hover preview before clicking
  • Custom initial camera focus point per map
  • Modal tag color, modal border color, globe base color, and country color overrides, plus three ready-made Modal Style Presets (Glass, Bento, Neon/Glow)
  • Choose whether pin images show as a full photo banner or a small logo mark
  • Growth Timeline mode – give pins a date and scrub through your company’s expansion year by year, with an optional autoplay
  • Pin List Sidebar – an always-visible, scrollable list of every pin alongside the map, with optional grouping and a search field for longer lists
  • Auto-Balance Layout – automatically shifts the globe to keep it clear of the open pin modal

Pro is a separate, small companion plugin that only ever hooks into the extension points this plugin exposes – it never modifies this plugin’s files, and everything you build on Free keeps working if you never upgrade.

Why not just embed Google Maps?

A standard map embed is flat and instantly familiar – which also means it doesn’t stand out. Granpai3DGlobe is built for the moment you want a homepage, “About us,” or locations page to feel a little more impressive: an actual rotating 3D sphere rendered in the browser, with your own pins, colors, and content – and no Google Maps API key or usage limits to manage.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/granpai3dglobe, or install directly through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to 3D Globe Maps > Add New Map in the admin sidebar, configure it, and add your pins.
  4. Copy the shortcode shown on the map’s edit screen into any post, page, or widget.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Google Maps API key?

No. Granpai3DGlobe doesn’t use Google Maps at all – the globe is rendered entirely with WebGL using open map data, so there’s no API key to obtain, no billing to monitor, and no risk of the map breaking if a key expires or a quota is hit.

Will this slow down my site?

The globe/map assets only load on pages that actually use the shortcode – there’s no sitewide overhead. The 3D rendering itself runs in the visitor’s browser via WebGL, which is hardware-accelerated on virtually all modern devices. If your map sits high up on a page (like a Hero section) and you want to squeeze out every last PageSpeed point, Settings > Performance has an optional “Aggressive lazy-load” toggle that delays the map’s scripts until a visitor scrolls near it – off by default, since the normal loading already works well for most sites.

Does this add any “Powered by” link or branding to my site?

Not unless you turn it on. There’s an optional, completely off-by-default credit link under Settings > Performance – nothing is added to your site’s frontend unless you explicitly opt in.

Does this work without a Pro license?

Yes. The Free plan includes 1 map with up to 5 pins, every render mode/theme/style, and the full Import/Export tools – enough to fully evaluate the plugin before deciding on Pro.

Can I use this as a store or office locator?

Yes – that’s one of the most common uses. Add one pin per location with its own address/contact details (Pro) or description text (Free), and each pin’s modal includes a “Get Directions” button pointing to that location on Google Maps.

Can I recolor the Photoreal globe style?

No – Photoreal uses a real satellite photo texture of Earth, which can’t be recolored as a flat color. The Minimal style (Pro) supports a custom globe base color instead.

What data does this plugin store, and where?

Maps and pins are stored as custom post types in your own WordPress database, like any other content – nothing is sent to or stored on an external server. The Import/Export tool lets you back up or move this data as a plain JSON file.

Where do I manage my Pro license?

Under 3D Globe Maps > Settings > License once the Pro add-on is installed and active.
sections.changelog:
2.10.0

  • Pro: Modal Style Presets – the pin pop-up modal can now use one of three ready-made looks (Glass, Bento, or Neon/Glow) instead of only individual color overrides, picked from Map Editor > Colors.
  • Fixed the admin Map Editor’s Live Preview showing the globe noticeably more zoomed-in than it actually appears on the frontend.

2.9.0

  • NEW: Flat map now supports the Dot Matrix and Low-Poly styles (previously only available on the 3D Globe) – a genuine, purpose-built rendering for the 2D map, not a reuse of the 3D version.
  • Replaced the flat map’s underlying country data with a higher-detail source (Natural Earth 1:50m, with Antarctica removed) for noticeably crisper, more accurate coastlines.
  • Fixed the globe sometimes rendering at a visibly different size right after the page loads compared to after clicking a pin or resizing the browser window – the camera’s zoom level is now computed consistently every time.
  • Redesigned how the pin modal decides whether to dock beside the map or sit flush against its edge into one consistent system, fixing a visible “jump” at certain screen widths.
  • Fixed Timeline mode’s control bar being hidden behind the pin modal on mobile.
  • Fixed the Timeline play/pause icon occasionally failing to render on some hosting setups – redrawn as pure CSS instead of an inline SVG, which is no longer dependent on the server not stripping it out.
  • Fixed several issues with the admin editor’s Live Preview panel: it no longer fails to load anything on the very first view, and correctly shows the Pin List Sidebar and Timeline bar without needing to change an unrelated setting first.
  • Fixed a subtle visual bug where a pin’s pulsing marker dot could sit slightly off-center from its own ripple ring.

2.8.4

  • Fixed the “Get Directions” button rendering as unstyled plain text – its styling had only ever existed in the Pro add-on’s own stylesheet, so a Free-only install never loaded it.
  • Fixed the pin modal visibly jumping in and out at the edges of the screen: it defaults to docking beside the map when the viewport has room for it, falling back to sitting flush against the map’s edge only when it genuinely doesn’t – decided once when the map loads (and again on window resize), never when opening a pin or clicking Next/Prev, which was the actual source of the jitter.
  • Capped the map’s own height at 80vh – without this, a map placed in a wide, full-width section could grow taller than the visible screen.

2.8.3

  • Fixed a loophole where importing a file with more maps than the Free plan allows, then restoring the extras from Trash, would bypass the map limit entirely – restoring an over-limit map now correctly sends it back to Trash with a clear explanation instead.
  • Added a warning on the Import screen when you’re already at the Free plan’s map limit, before importing causes any confusion.

2.8.2

  • Fixed Import/Export not including the “Get Directions” toggle per pin, and the modal side (left/right) per map – both were silently reset to their default on import.

2.8.1

  • Fixed the “Enable aggressive lazy-load” checkbox on Settings > Performance not saving – it had lost its Save button when the new credit-link setting was added in 2.8.0.
  • Both Performance tab toggles now use the same animated switch style as the rest of the plugin, instead of a plain checkbox.

2.8.0

  • Flight-line arc and Next/Previous pin navigation are now core Free functionality (previously required Pro) – on by default, giving every Free install a more compelling, shareable demo out of the box.
  • Fixed a bug where the modal’s nav row (needed for both Get Directions and Prev/Next) never rendered at all on a pure Free install without Pro installed.
  • Added a “Support” link on the Plugins list screen, pointing to the WordPress.org support forum.
  • Added an optional, off-by-default “Powered by Granpai3DGlobe” credit link in the pin modal (Settings > Performance) – opt-in only, per WordPress.org’s plugin guidelines.
  • Redesigned the “Upgrade to Pro” banners shown throughout the admin to be more visually distinct, and switched them to open Freemius’s checkout directly.
  • Fixed the docked pin modal being cut off (and the globe appearing oddly shifted) in the admin Map Settings live preview.
  • Fixed the modal title being nearly invisible in the admin live preview due to a missing color rule.

2.7.0

  • Free plan pin limit raised from 2 to 5 pins per map.
  • Added a “Get Directions” toggle for every pin (on by default) – auto-builds a Google Maps link from the pin’s own coordinates.
  • Pro: the Get Directions button now supports a fully custom link and button text, so it can point anywhere – a website, an article – not just Google Maps.
  • Pro: added an “Autoplay on page load” toggle for Timeline maps (Map Settings > Timeline). Heads up if you already use Timeline: this replaces timeline auto-play previously starting unconditionally the moment Timeline was enabled – the new toggle defaults to off, so existing Timeline maps will need it turned on again to keep auto-playing.
  • Every “Upgrade to Pro” link across the plugin now opens Freemius’s checkout directly, instead of occasionally landing on a broken page.
  • Free now shows every Pro feature as a preview (grayed out, with its real label) instead of simply not rendering it, so it’s clear what upgrading unlocks.

2.6.1

  • Fixed the “See Pro” upgrade button in Settings > License not opening a working checkout – now uses Freemius’s Checkout widget directly, with both Annual and Lifetime plans selectable.
  • Fixed a licensing-menu configuration issue that could show “Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page” right after connecting to Freemius on first activation.
  • Updated the bundled Freemius SDK to the latest version.
  • Hardened the data passed to Pro’s extension hooks with an extra layer of sanitization.

2.6.0

  • Redesigned pin clustering: overlapping pins are no longer hidden behind a single marker with a count badge – every pin now stays visible and individually clickable, fanned out in a small arc.
  • Fixed several sources of erratic modal/navigation behavior in the admin Map Settings live preview, including stale event listeners and false-positive pin clustering.
  • Added a “Clone” row action on the Globe Maps list to duplicate a map together with all its pins.
  • Added a Zoom on/off toggle for 3D Globe mode.
  • Various fixes to pin modal positioning and sizing on wide or docked layouts.

2.1.0

  • Added a live preview to the Map editor screen.
  • Added a custom initial camera focus point per map.
  • Pro features now pause cleanly (without losing saved data) if a license lapses, instead of showing stale data.

2.0.0

  • Rebuilt around a Map + Pin data model (previously a single shortcode with attributes).
  • Added Flat map mode, Light theme, and Minimal globe style.
  • Added Import / Export.
  • Added the Pro add-on.
